reasons: Rule applies: Commerce One is a licensor/hosting provider supplying the MarketSite Service plus installation, support and training and handling Corio/Customer data, so the playbook expects an insurance covenant; the cited Miscellaneous (§14) and the surrounding paragraphs contain no coverage undertaking, supporting the 'missing' classification.

The inserted covenant is directionally correct (obligation runs against the counterparty, benefits our client Corio as licensee) and matches the preferred position on all material terms: CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where Customer/Corio data is processed, workers' compensation as required by law, and certificates on request, with a survival tail of one year.

Placement in the general/miscellaneous section immediately before the entire-agreement/signature paragraph follows the redline guidance, and no existing acceptable insurance clause is being over-flagged.
Comment is accurate, concise, states what changed and why, cites the playbook position and offers the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback.

Minor cleanup only (not fail-worthy): the new section duplicates the existing 14.10 number and the trailing meta-sentence 'The subsequent Section of this Section 14 shall be renumbered accordingly.' is drafting instruction text that should not sit in the operative agreement — renumber the insert as 14.11 (or renumber Complete Understanding) and delete that sentence.
